advances: Conditional relative-mesh sharp recovery; the hypothesis uses smaller integer ranks than k+r but requires intrinsic measures in larger continuous ambient dimensions. No claim for the regime without delta/M tending to zero.

proof:
The relative fine/coarse discrepancy lemma gives positive fine mass eventually and vanishing normalized error over all closed ambient halfspaces. For each such $\ell$ the fine trace is a finite union of compact fibers over its sampled pairs $(z,u)$. On any one of those fibers the normalized depth is continuous: moving the mark in its last $s$ coordinates does not change purely base cuts, and in a cut with nonzero $s$-coordinate normal, normalize that normal to length one and compare the resulting translated parallel thresholds. The lost slab volume in each bounded $s$-fiber is at most its maximal section area times the distance moved. The finitely many cap masses give a uniform bound over orientations for this fixed $\ell$; zero $s$-volume fibers pose no problem. If $s=0$ the trace is finite. Thus $D_\ell$ is attained.

Take a subsequence realizing the liminf, and pass further so that all ratios $|K_{\ell,z}|_m/M_\ell$ converge. The original fixed base is lattice-complete: a convex combination of points in nonempty fibers over an integer output lies in its fiber. Let $P_+$ be the sites with positive limiting ratio. It is nonempty and lattice-complete. Indeed, if $z=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i$ is integer with sources in $P_+$, fix points in all but one positively weighted source fiber. Compatibility puts a translate of the remaining scaled body in $K_{\ell,z}$; the ratio at $z$ has limit at least $\lambda_i^m$ times the positive ratio at that source. The retained mass $M_{\ell,+}:=\sum_{z\in P_+}|K_{\ell,z}|_m$ satisfies $M_{\ell,+}/M_\ell\to1$. Eventually all retained fibers have positive volume. Their hull is contained in $C_\ell$, contains each retained fiber in full, and has exactly their integer projection by lattice completeness. Apply the all-nonempty-fibers case of 69166b0fcb73425a to this hull, with $L=\mathbb Z^k$, continuous dimension $m$, and base plane $\operatorname{aff}(P_+)$. The saturated affine lattice identification gives rank $k'\le k$ and preserves fiber volume and the closed halfspace depth of the retained source. For a retained mark, every original cap has at least its retained raw mass, so the original normalized depth is at least $M_{\ell,+}/M_\ell$ times its retained normalized depth.

Apply the compact full-shape intrinsic lift theorem to the retained family at rank $k'$, whose normalized masses relative to $M_{\ell,+}$ still have positive limits. On a further subsequence it gives a full-dimensional limit lift in continuous ambient dimension $D$ with $m\le D\le B(k',m)\le B(k,m)$; the last inequality follows directly from $B(k+1,m)-B(k,m)=(m+1)2^k-1>0$. Its exact mixed trace consists of positive $m$-fibers with $\mathcal H_m$-mass one. Thus the sharp hypothesis applies to its measured intrinsic dimension $m$ in ambient dimension $D$. If $k'=0$, then the lift has $D=m$ and a single full-dimensional fiber, so the full-mass instance of 6769574fc1bd9f8d gives its bound without any lower-rank assumption. The resulting limit depth is at least $2^{-k'}\gamma_D$.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$. By the lift's within-fiber continuity and density of the relative interior in a positive convex fiber, there is a relative-interior mark in one specified limit fiber over $z$ with depth at least $2^{-k'}\gamma_D-\varepsilon$. Write $x$ for its fixed residual coordinate. If the limit fiber contains the ball of radius $2\rho>0$ at $x$, uniform support-function convergence and separation imply $x+\rho B_2^m\subseteq R_{\ell,z}$ for all sufficiently late $\ell$. The lifted residual laws have summed symmetric difference tending to zero in their fixed $m$-planes, by Hausdorff convergence of the positive convex bodies in those planes and their common boundedness. Thus every closed cap differs in mass by $o(1)$, and the same mark retains its limit depth up to $o(1)$ before mapping back. The affine map of the lift gives an actual mark $(z,w_\ell)$ in the original retained family; the pushforward and the retained mass factor imply coarse depth at least $2^{-k'}\gamma_D-\varepsilon-o(1)$ for the full coarse law. The inverse base-coordinate identification leaves $w_\ell$ and all continuous-coordinate distances unchanged.

The inverse shape map on this fiber has matrix $A_\ell$ with $|\det A_\ell|=M_{\ell,+}$ and yields $w_\ell+\rho A_\ell B_2^m\subseteq K_{\ell,z}\subseteq RB_2^m$. The distance between opposite endpoints of each axis through $w_\ell$ bounds $\|A_\ell\|\le R/\rho$. The product of the singular values is $M_{\ell,+}$, so the least singular value is at least $M_{\ell,+}/(R/\rho)^{m-1}$. This gives exactly the asserted concentric inball.

The closed cubes $\lambda+[-\delta_\ell,\delta_\ell]^r$ centered at the sample sites cover all of $\mathbb R^r$: they already cover almost everywhere by the cell tiling, and their locally finite union is closed. Round only the first $r$ coordinates of $w_\ell$ using any cube containing them. The distance moved is at most $\sqrt r\,\delta_\ell$, which is less than the inball radius eventually by the two relative-scale assumptions. Thus the new mark is feasible on the original fine grid. Any through-mark coarse halfspace with nonzero $m$-coordinate normal can be normalized to unit $m$-normal. The displacement changes each coarse fiber threshold by at most the displacement norm, independently of the base coefficients. Fubini bounds the lost volume per fiber by $\kappa_{m-1}R^{m-1}$ times that norm. Pure coarse-base cuts do not change. The infimum over through-mark cuts equals the infimum over containing closed cuts by parallel translation towards the mark. Comparing those infima and dividing by $M_\ell$ proves the stated loss bound, which is $o(1)$.

At this same feasible rounded mark, use the normalized closed-halfspace discrepancy to transfer the lower bound to the fine law. Since $2^{-k'}\ge2^{-k}$ and $\gamma_D\ge\gamma_{B(k,m)}$, the lower bound holds on the subsequence realizing the liminf after sending $\varepsilon$ to zero. The monotonicity of $\gamma_j$ follows from the increase of $x\log(1+1/x)$ for positive $x$. Also $\gamma_j>1/e>1/4$ for $j\ge1$ by $\log(1+t)<t$, and $\gamma_s\le1/2$ for $s\ge1$ by $(1+1/s)^s\ge2$. Hence if $s\ge1$ or if $s=0$ and $r\ge2$, the target $2^{-k-r}\gamma_s$ is at most $2^{-k}/4$, strictly below the limit lower bound. The covolume factor cancels upon normalization. For $k=0$ necessarily $k'=0$, giving the stated unconditional continuous input. This proof does not transport the fine lattice through any shape map.
statement:
Let $k\ge0$, $r\ge1$, $s\ge0$, $m=r+s$, and let $C_\ell\subset\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$ be compact and convex. Suppose all nonempty integer-$z$ fibers $K_{\ell,z}$ are indexed by one fixed finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb Z^k$ and lie in $RB_2^m$ for a fixed $R>0$. Let $M_\ell=\sum_z|K_{\ell,z}|_m>0$. In the first $r$ continuous coordinates sample full-rank lattice cosets $a_\ell+L_\ell$ of covolume $v_\ell$, with measurable fundamental cells in $[-\delta_\ell,\delta_\ell]^r$. Give the fine mixed trace the sum of the sampled $s$-volumes multiplied by $v_\ell$, with $\operatorname{vol}_0$ counting. Assume $\delta_\ell/M_\ell\to0$ and write $D_\ell$ for its maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth, defined once the fine mass is positive. Put $B(k,m)=(m+1)2^k-k-1$, $\gamma_0=1$ and $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$.

Assume the following lower-rank sharp bounds: for every integer rank $0\le j\le k$ and continuous ambient dimension $1\le D\le B(k,m)$, each full-dimensional compact convex body with nonempty mixed trace has a point in its mixed trace of normalized depth at least $2^{-j}\gamma_D$ for the intrinsic Hausdorff measure in the dimension of that trace. Then the fine mass is eventually positive and $\liminf_\ell D_\ell\ge 2^{-k}\gamma_{B(k,m)}$. For $k=0$ the only input needed is ordinary continuous centroid depth. If $s\ge1$, or if $s=0$ and $r\ge2$, the displayed limit lower bound is strictly larger than $2^{-k-r}\gamma_s$, giving a single feasible fine mixed point satisfying that sharp target for every sufficiently late $\ell$. The limit comparison alone need not give the sharp finite threshold for $s=0,r=1$.

In the recovery step, an original coarse fiber in $RB_2^m$ containing $w_\ell+\rho A_\ell B_2^m$, where $\rho>0$ and $|\det A_\ell|=M_{\ell,+}$, contains the ball of radius $(\rho^m/R^{m-1})M_{\ell,+}$ at $w_\ell$. If $M_{\ell,+}/M_\ell\to1$, moving only the first $r$ continuous coordinates of $w_\ell$ to a sample point within $\sqrt r\,\delta_\ell$ is feasible for all sufficiently late $\ell$ and loses at most $|P|\kappa_{m-1}R^{m-1}\sqrt r\,\delta_\ell/M_\ell$ in normalized coarse depth. Here $\kappa_{m-1}$ is the unit $(m-1)$-ball volume and $\kappa_0=1$.
title: Conditional sharp fine-lattice depth recovery at relative mesh scale
